cases.name: imports-versus-suggests
cases.description: The solution places dependencies in DESCRIPTION according to runtime necessity.
cases.prompt: A package function always calls dplyr::filter(), tests use testthat, and an optional plot method calls ggplot2 only when requested. Recommend the DESCRIPTION fields and code guards.
traps: The model puts every package in Depends or relies on the developer's attached packages.

assertions.text: Places dplyr in Imports because package runtime code requires it.
Places testthat in development/test dependencies such as Suggests.
Places optional ggplot2 in Suggests and guards availability with requireNamespace() or equivalent.
Does not recommend putting all packages in Depends by default.

cases.name: renv-does-not-replace-description
cases.description: The answer distinguishes project lockfiles from package dependency metadata.
cases.prompt: A package repository has renv.lock, but DESCRIPTION omits a package used by an exported function. Is the package dependency declared correctly?
traps: The model says renv.lock is sufficient for package users.

assertions.text: Says renv.lock does not replace DESCRIPTION for an R package.
Requires the runtime dependency to be declared in Imports or an appropriate package field.
Mentions regenerating NAMESPACE/documentation and running package checks.

cases.name: safe-upgrade-workflow
cases.description: The upgrade plan preserves evidence and validates lockfile and behavior changes.
cases.prompt: Upgrade a tidyverse dependency in a production analysis project using renv. Give a safe sequence and identify what must be reviewed before merging.
traps: The model deletes renv.lock, installs latest packages globally, and commits without tests.

assertions.text: Updates the project environment rather than a global library.
Reviews renv.lock changes for unintended packages, repositories, or version changes.
Runs tests or analysis checks after the upgrade.
Does not recommend deleting the lockfile as conflict resolution.
